tasks.short: Check billing data against delivery evidence, agreed prices and tax rules, then correct errors.

steps.what: Retrieve billing records and delivery records from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Compare supporting documents in the {DOCS} with billing quantities and agreed terms.

loop.input: Service confirmation and pricing agreement with source references.
loop.output: Referenced quantities, prices, dates and relevant billing terms.
loop.check: Validate field types, units, arithmetic and source locations; flag ambiguous or conflicting terms.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; unresolved fields go to the billing clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Some supporting evidence contains free text and variable layouts without structured equivalents.

steps.what: Check prices, quantities, duplicates and tax calculations in the {ERP}.
Clarify missing evidence or disputed terms with the service owner through the {EMAIL}.
Review corrections and update the billing record in the {ERP}.

tasks.design: An integration joins records from the {ERP} and {OPS_SYSTEM}, while configured checks identify billing discrepancies. A bounded extractor reads unstructured evidence in the {DOCS}; the billing clerk resolves ambiguity and approves proposed corrections before the {ERP} changes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Delivery evidence, commercial terms and billing records use different references. Existing checks often cover arithmetic but miss missing evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing validation features and cheaper integration development can connect those records. Bounded extraction can handle residual documents without controlling postings.
tasks.still_hard: Missing delivery evidence and disputed agreements still need people. Issued invoices may require credit notes rather than direct edits.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when apparently correct numbers misrepresent the service delivered, and settle the facts with its owner.

ambition.what: Daily prioritisation of recurring billing defects by value and source.

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends more time resolving causes of disputed billing and less time comparing fields. Delegated authority could include prioritising source-data fixes; commercial concessions remain with their current approvers.

reach.learn: Credit-note accounting, revenue cut-off and how billing defects affect ledger balances.

evidence.claim: Configured arithmetic, duplicate and reference checks suit structured billing records.
AFAS Profit extracts supplier invoice data; this supports document capture feasibility, not outgoing billing accuracy.

assumptions: Step shares estimate a typical mixed goods-and-services workflow, not measured customer time.
Most billing data is structured; document review and missing evidence explain the remaining manual work.
Build ranges estimate one billing flow with supported exports or interfaces and exclude procurement delays.
The access range includes privacy review and consultation assessment; national rules may require longer consultation.
unknowns: Available interfaces and shared references between billing and delivery records.
Actual discrepancy volumes and their causes.
Whether national rules require employee consultation for the proposed change.
research_questions: Which existing {ERP} checks can be enabled before building additional rules?
Which document fields remain necessary after structured evidence is connected?
new_work: Review extracted evidence and unresolved discrepancies.
Maintain billing checks and approved correction mappings.
Monitor failed joins and inspect a sample of passed checks.

tasks.short: Prepare itemised invoices, approve their release and record customer amounts due.

steps.what: Select approved billable deliveries or services from the {OPS_SYSTEM} for the {ERP}.
Apply customer prices, discounts and payment terms in the {ERP}.
Calculate line amounts, tax and totals in the {ERP}.
Generate an itemised draft invoice in the {ERP}.
Review the draft invoice and approve release in the {ERP}.
Issue the approved invoice through the {ERP}.
Post the customer amount due in the {ERP}.

tasks.design: An integration brings approved billable events from the {OPS_SYSTEM} into the {ERP}, which applies prices, calculates tax and generates invoices. Recorded release approval permits dispatch and receivable posting; duplicate controls and delivery status support safe retries.
tasks.previous_blocker: Billable events and customer terms were not consistently linked. Staff filled gaps between existing invoice features and operational records.
tasks.enabler_now: Most calculation and invoice functions already exist. Faster integration development makes connecting the remaining inputs cheaper.
tasks.still_hard: Complex tax treatment, milestone acceptance and negotiated exceptions need finance judgement. Invoice format and reporting requirements depend on transaction dates and national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether the evidence supports charging the customer and recognise commercially sensitive exceptions.

ambition.what: A daily unbilled-delivery report for service owners.

tasks.altitude: Routine preparation becomes a monitored flow, leaving the clerk time to investigate unbilled work and failed deliveries. Invoice approval and concession rights do not automatically expand.

reach.task: Investigate customer disputes caused by invoice content.
reach.learn: Customer delivery requirements, dispute categories and payment-term interpretation.

evidence.claim: Price application, tax arithmetic, invoice generation and receivable posting are established configurable finance functions.
The proposed effort and remaining review time are design estimates, not documented case results.

assumptions: Approved prices and tax codes are maintained as structured records.
The representative workflow uses supervisor release approval; actual approval policies vary.
Dispatch requires the recorded approval from s5 and cannot bypass it.
Posting and issue may be one transaction in the {ERP}; they are separated here by their outputs.
Build ranges cover one invoice flow, including access review and assessment of consultation under national rules.
unknowns: Current invoice channels, formats and customer requirements.
Which release approvals are required today.
Supported posting, dispatch and retry controls.
Applicable tax scenarios and national e-invoicing requirements.
research_questions: Can configured {ERP} billing consume approved operational events directly?
How will duplicate invoice prevention work across interrupted dispatch and posting?
new_work: Maintain invoice templates, prices and tax mappings.
Handle rejected deliveries and incomplete billable events.
Review approval summaries and reconcile issued invoices to receivables.

tasks.short: Link invoices to supporting evidence and maintain complete, retrievable billing records.

steps.what: Locate delivery evidence and service confirmations in the {DOCS}.
Match supporting evidence to the invoice record in the {ERP}.
File invoice copies and supporting documents in the {DOCS}.
Request missing evidence from service owners through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: A deterministic integration joins issued invoices in the {ERP} to evidence in the {DOCS} using exact transaction references. Configured filing applies access and retention metadata, while the {WORKFLOW} queues missing or ambiguous evidence for the billing clerk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Documents were filed separately from transactions, with inconsistent references and ownership. Manual filing concealed incomplete evidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing document features and small integrations can capture references at source and test completeness automatically.
tasks.still_hard: Historical documents may lack reliable identifiers. Retention, legal holds and access must follow GDPR and applicable national rules.
tasks.human_edge: Judge whether evidence actually substantiates the charge and obtain missing context from the responsible person.

ambition.what: An invoice evidence pack for collection disputes.

tasks.altitude: The clerk handles incomplete records and prepares dispute evidence instead of routinely filing documents. Retention and deletion authority stays with existing owners.

reach.task: Retrieve evidence for a sampled revenue transaction.
reach.learn: Evidence sufficiency, document provenance, retention and audit sampling.

evidence.claim: Exact-reference linking, metadata filing and completeness queues can use deterministic software without a model.
GDPR requires appropriate access and storage controls where billing evidence contains personal data.

assumptions: New documents can receive stable transaction identifiers at source.
Automatic linking accepts exact references only; ambiguous matches remain unresolved.
The service owner is usually internal; the clerk may also request evidence from an external service provider.
The design applies approved retention metadata and does not introduce automatic deletion.
Build ranges cover new records; a historical archive cleanup is separate.
Access estimates include privacy review and any consultation assessment required by national rules.
unknowns: Document locations, identifiers and historical archive quality.
Approved retention periods and legal-hold processes.
Whether current {DOCS} permissions match billing confidentiality needs.
How often missing evidence requires external contact.
research_questions: Can document references be attached when delivery or service completion is recorded?
Which evidence types are mandatory for each invoice category?
new_work: Resolve missing and ambiguous document links.
Maintain evidence requirements and access mappings.
Check archive completeness, retrieval and legal-hold behaviour.

tasks.short: Use calculation tools and billing screens to total figures and enter billing amounts.

steps.what: Calculate billing totals in the {SPREADSHEET} from approved billing data.
Key calculated billing amounts into the {ERP}.

tasks.design: Remove the separate calculation sheet and rekeying once the invoice flow calculates directly from approved records in the {ERP}. Retain configured reconciliation checks in the {ERP}; invoice review and release remain in the invoice-preparation workflow.
tasks.previous_blocker: Disconnected operational inputs encouraged a separate calculation sheet that became part of routine billing.
tasks.enabler_now: The connected invoice flow can calculate and retain the same figures without a second manual calculation.
tasks.still_hard: Undocumented formulas may contain valid pricing exceptions. They must be understood before the sheet is retired.
tasks.human_edge: Identify hidden commercial rules and decide whether a familiar workaround still serves a valid control purpose.
tasks.altitude: Separate calculation and rekeying disappear from the week. This removal alone grants no new decision rights.

reach.task: Reconcile billed totals to receivable postings.
reach.learn: Control totals, duplicate prevention and reconciliation exceptions.

evidence.claim: The legacy equipment task commonly survives as keyboard entry and separate calculation work.
A separate calculation and rekeying step can disappear when the invoice flow performs the same controlled arithmetic.

assumptions: This describes the residual workaround where it exists; many companies already perform calculations entirely in the {ERP}.
Elimination removes separate human operations, not the underlying arithmetic.
The invoice-preparation implementation is a prerequisite; these ranges cover incremental retirement work only.
This task overlaps invoice preparation and verification; its savings must not be counted twice.
No incremental runtime service or employee monitoring is introduced.
unknowns: Whether separate calculation or rekeying still occurs.
Which formulas encode exceptions absent from the {ERP}.
Whether the calculation sheet supports any independent control that must be replaced.
Who authorises retirement of the current procedure.
research_questions: Does each existing formula have an equivalent configured billing rule or necessary control?
Can the independent reconciliation use source totals without recreating manual arithmetic?
new_work: Document migrated exceptions and update the billing procedure.

role.altitude: The role shifts toward resolving billing evidence gaps, investigating recurring defects and supporting disputes. Broader authority over source-data fixes or billing holds requires explicit delegation; commercial and accounting approvals remain assigned.
reach: Support accountants with explanations of recurring revenue adjustments.
Support collectors with complete invoice evidence packs.
Support bookkeeping clerks with reconciled billing and receivable totals.
skills_to_grow: Billing rules, tax codes and credit-note controls.
Transaction references, reconciliation and exception analysis.
Evidence quality, GDPR access controls and retention.
Testing configured rules and reviewing bounded extraction outputs.
role.ambitious_version: A billing operations specialist who identifies unbilled work, prioritises recurring defects with service owners and supplies reliable evidence for customer disputes.
